title: Permission Probe & Audit Snapshot Regression Suite
creator: Samuel Rivera
description: Build a repeatable regression suite that validates RBAC v2 permission enforcement and audit log integrity by comparing 'audit snapshots' derived from production-like fixtures to a verified canonical baseline. This ticket owns the probe harness, snapshot serializer, and nightly regression pipeline that detects behavioral drift (permission regressions, missing audit events, SAML-related edge cases) and emits actionable diffs for on-call and platform owners.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A probe harness that can synthesize 10k permission checks across roles and resources and produce an audit snapshot in the agreed JSONL format
2) Nightly CI job that compares generated snapshots against a canonical baseline and fails the job on non-whitelisted diffs
3) Diff output includes per-check classification (policy mismatch | missing-audit | unexpected-allow | unexpected-deny) and a reproducible test vector to reproduce locally
4) Less than 0.5% flakiness in repeated runs with masked production fixtures; persistent flakiness has a documented mitigation path
5) On failure: automated GitHub issue template with failing vectors, stack traces, and relevant links (PRs, dashboards, recent deploys)
6) Integration with alerting: Slack #rbac-regressions channel and PagerDuty routing for P0-like regressions affecting production roles
test_plan: A) Implement snapshot serializer v1 (fields: check_id, actor, resource, action, result, timestamp, audit_event_id, context_tags)
B) Create a fixture generator that masks PII and generates role bindings from prod-like templates (K8s rolebindings, console role grants, SSO group mappings)
C) Run the harness against local devstack and then run in CI using a small gated fleet of staging tenants
D) Validate diff engine: run golden->generated comparisons and assert classification rules across 50 seeded variants
E) Add fuzz runner that mutates role conditions and asserts the harness flags regressions without false positives
technical_notes: Design decisions: use a compact JSONL snapshot format to simplify streaming diffs and make both storage and triage fast. Snapshot hashing will use canonical key ordering and stable timestamps (rounded) to reduce noise. We'll piggyback on the existing synthetic-traffic harness (ENG-31724) to generate permission checks; however we must add SAML-specific flows (group-to-role mapping jitter, nameID formats) to catch recent SSO integration regressions. The snapshot schema is versioned (schema_v1) and migration notes will be included in docs. We will store golden baselines in an immutable S3 prefix with signed metadata and expose them in the Console for audits.
